whyThisShow: This is a Wall of Sound-era show with an officially released soundboard (Dave's Picks Vol. 17), and the community keeps returning to it for the second-set sequence that starts with Weather Report Suite and runs through Spanish Jam, Eyes of the World, and China Doll. One reviewer called it "one of the most powerful passages in the history or Western civilization" [source: 'One of the most powerful passages in the history or Western civilization. The Let it Grow is furious. Manic. Perfect.']. The Weather Report Suite in particular draws outsized praise, with one listener calling it "the hands down winner for best ever" [source: 'the WRS is the hands down winner for best ever, and the Spanish is also easily the best of the many in '74']. The first set holds up on its own terms too, with Scarlet Begonias drawing notice for Garcia deploying "some sick distortion for the first part of the jam" — something one listener said they hadn't heard in another version [source: 'JG kicks in some sick distortion for the first part of the jam; can\'t say i\'ve heard another example of that before']. There is one known tape flaw: a cut in Let It Grow and an audience-sourced "One More Saturday Night" closer [source: 'My only complaint is there is a cut in LIG, and considering OMSN is Aud, there might be a patch out there for this hole?'].
listenFor: Start with the Weather Report Suite into Let It Grow — reviewers describe the Let It Grow as "furious" and "manic," with Garcia and Lesh intertwining "like lightning and thunder" [source: 'Garcia and Lesh intertwine like lightning and thunder']. The Spanish Jam that follows is led by Lesh, and one listener warned it is "quite scary for the uninitiated" and recommended that new fans "probably wait a bit before listening to something this heavy, this thick" [source: 'new fans should probably wait a bit before listening to something this heavy, this thick. It can be quite scary for the uninitiated']. Phil's playing is a through-line worth tracking across the whole show — one reviewer noted a "spectacular Playin' where phil really lets loose," then added that the second set is "nothing compared to the ridiculous 2nd set, where he just goes crazy" [source: 'a spectacular Playin\' where phil really lets loose. which is nothing compared to the ridiculous 2nd set, where he just goes crazy']. The first-set Scarlet Begonias is worth a separate listen for the unusual Garcia distortion tone [source: 'JG kicks in some sick distortion for the first part of the jam; can\'t say i\'ve heard another example of that before'].
context: July 1974 falls squarely in the Wall of Sound touring period, when the Dead were running the massive custom PA system built by Owsley and the crew. This show at Selland Arena in Fresno was released officially as Dave's Picks Vol. 17, putting it in a small group of '74 dates that received the band's direct endorsement. The best-circulating recording is a soundboard (identifier: gd74-07-19.sbd.symons.12381.sbeok.shnf). One listener noted that by this point in the summer, the material was sounding "completely different than what was happening on tour in May-June" [source: '8/6/74 IMO sounds completely different than what was happening on tour in May-June, and so to does this date'].
funFact: One listener noted that on the China Doll, "jerry kinda toys with the mars hotel opening notes" — a bit of in-show self-reference that makes this version worth comparing to the studio recording [source: 'china doll is grown up a bit, jerry kinda toys with the mars hotel opening notes'].
headline: Phil owns the second set, Fresno, July '74.
